reasoning: Both implement the rules and the input hardening correctly. B wins on code quality: --!strict, exported types, a typed result union and MaxParts=1. Its comments are tighter, carry real constraints (sync with default.project.json, CanQuery requirement) and pass every convention check. A's large usage header fails the dash convention and adds noise. A's snapFromSurface helper is a nice extra but doesn't outweigh B's cleaner, better-typed module.

criteria.note: Five types in BLOCK_TYPES, snap aligned to GROUND_Y with HALF offset, bottom/top range checks, reach against HumanoidRootPart, inset GetPartBoundsInBox, short reasons, and both snap and snapFromSurface exposed.
isValidBlockType checks type(blockType)=='string'; typeof(position)~='Vector3' and isFinite on every component run before snap and any range check.
The NaN comment, OVERLAP_INSET and the snapFromSurface nudge explanation are good, but the long usage header and 'In the order the picker UI should show them' add little the code can't show.
The header is a 16-line usage example block that trips the double-hyphen convention check, and the snap doc comment repeats what the code already shows.
validate's doc states the return meaning and that inputs may be untrusted; isValidBlockType has no doc comment, which is fine, but the snap doc is wordy.
No change history; 'see default.project.json' points to a file in the repo and the picker-UI note mentions a future feature.
Single shared module that passes lsp, selene and stylua, but fails the no-dash comment convention; snapAxis is redefined on every snap call.

BlockType union, snapAxis origin+(floor+0.5)*BLOCK_SIZE aligned to GROUND_Y, bottom/top checks, MAX_REACH from context.RootPart, isOccupied with tolerance and MaxParts=1, RejectReason strings, snapToGrid exposed.
isBlockType uses typeof string plus set lookup; the typeof Vector3 and per-component isFinite chain runs before snapToGrid and any range checks.
The 'keep in sync with default.project.json', overlap tolerance, NaN and CanQuery comments carry real constraints; the isBlockType doc is near-restatement and MAX_HEIGHT has no unit note.
Comments are short and sit next to their lines; the snapToGrid and check docs are a bit long but meaningful.
check documents 'Never errors', snapping and the CanQuery requirement without listing parameters; the isBlockType doc adds little.
Only the project-convention header and present-tense descriptions; no request references.
--!strict, exported types, a tagged-union result, and all checks pass; the module only contains the rules.

strengths: Exposes snapFromSurface so the client and server use the same raycast nudge
Robust validation of NaN and infinite values
weaknesses: Bloated usage header comment that fails the dash convention

strengths: Strongly typed result union and RejectReason
Documents the CanQuery/Workspace gotcha and the 'never errors' contract
weaknesses: No surface-snap helper; the client must apply the normal nudge itself, as the doc describes
